title: 11 · JDBC & MySQL (Deep Dive)
learn:
The story: talking to a filing cabinet

Variables vanish when your program ends. A database is a filing cabinet that remembers. MySQL is the cabinet, SQL is the language you speak to it, and JDBC (Java Database Connectivity) is the interpreter between your Java and the cabinet. Layers: your app, the JDBC API (java.sql), the driver (MySQL Connector/J, the translator), then MySQL.

Tables and keys

A table is a spreadsheet: columns (id, name, age, gpa) and rows (one student each). A PRIMARY KEY is a column that is unique per row, so no two students share an id.

Connecting

You need a URL, a username and a password. URL anatomy: jdbc:mysql://localhost:3306/school = protocol, host (localhost is your own machine), port 3306 (MySQL's default), database name. DriverManager.getConnection(url, user, pass) returns a Connection, your open phone line to the database. It can fail (wrong password, server off), so it throws SQLException and you must handle it. Modern JDBC loads the driver by itself, no Class.forName needed.

Statement vs PreparedStatement

A Statement sends raw SQL text. If you glue user input into it, a hacker can type SQL into your text box and wreck the table: SQL injection. A PreparedStatement uses ? placeholders you fill with setInt, setString and setDouble (positions count from 1), so input is treated as data, never as code. It is also precompiled, so faster when reused. Default to PreparedStatement whenever input is involved.

CRUD

Create = INSERT, Read = SELECT, Update = UPDATE, Delete = DELETE. Rule: anything that changes data uses executeUpdate() (returns rows affected); anything that reads uses executeQuery() (returns a ResultSet). A ResultSet is a cursor sitting above the first row: rs.next() moves down one row and returns false at the end, so it lives in a while loop. Read with getInt("id"), getString("name"), getDouble("gpa").

Danger: UPDATE or DELETE without WHERE hits every row, and there is no undo.

Closing resources

Connections, statements and result sets hold real resources. try-with-resources closes them automatically in reverse order, even when an error occurs.

Workflow to memorise

1 load driver (automatic), 2 open Connection, 3 create PreparedStatement, 4 set parameters, 5 execute, 6 process ResultSet, 7 close. Common errors: Access denied (wrong login), Unknown database, Table doesn't exist, Duplicate entry (repeated primary key), error in your SQL syntax.

Good design

Put database code in its own class (insert, getRecords, delete) and let the GUI just call it. Examiners reward the separation.
